title: Pull-back preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice's inputs drawn from $X$, Bob's inputs from $Y$, and outputs in $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be maps re-indexing the two input types. Then the pull-back protocol over $X'$ and $Y'$ obtained by pre-composing each of Alice's message functions with $f_X$ and each of Bob's message functions with $f_Y$ has the same communication complexity as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: a deterministic protocol p over input types X, Y with output type alpha
a re-indexing map f_X : X' → X for Alice's inputs
a re-indexing map f_Y : Y' → Y for Bob's inputs
replaced:
For any protocol $p$ over $X \times Y$ and input maps $f_X : X' \to X$, $f_Y : Y' \to Y$,
\[
  (p.\texttt{comap}\;f_X\;f_Y).\texttt{complexity} \;=\; p.\texttt{complexity}.
\]
